title: Client-driven snapshot reconciliation and hybrid reconnect arbitration for SSE streaming
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our SSE streaming clients sometimes rejoin after network interruptions and receive out-of-order or duplicate chunks, which breaks downstream tool/function call boundaries and structured JSON outputs. Existing resume-token approaches are brittle for multiplexed sessions and increase server memory pressure when checkpoints are kept per-client for long periods.

Goal: Introduce a hybrid reconnect arbitration that combines a compact client snapshot (local sequence window + last-complete-toolcall id) with a server-side short-lived ephemeral resume anchor. The server will attempt deterministic reconciliation using sequence numbers and idempotency markers; when ambiguity remains, the protocol falls back to a conservative replay with client-side merge heuristics. The design must preserve function-call atomicity, protect structured JSON boundaries across fragmented chunks, and stay compatible with current HTTP SSE and our eventstream framing shims.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Clients can attach a compact snapshot header on reconnect containing: last_seq_received, last_complete_toolcall_id, and a 32-bit rolling hash of the last N bytes.
2) Server replies with either a resume_anchor token (short TTL) or a reconciliation decision (resume_point + drop list).
3) When server issues a resume_anchor, the client resumes from the anchor; when server issues a reconciliation decision, client trims local buffer per instructions and resumes.
4) Tool/function calls maintain atomic boundaries: either replay completes or server instructs a rollback to the last complete toolcall.
5) End-to-end tests show median replay latency < 15ms and no structural JSON corruption in 99.99% of simulated reconnects.
6) Backwards compatibility: legacy clients (no snapshot header) should still work and receive best-effort resume_anchor behavior.
7) Documentation and SDKs updated with examples and edge-case guidance.
implementation_notes:
- Add an Opt-In reconnect header: X-RW-Snapshot: base64({last_seq,last_toolcall,window_hash,flags}). Keep header size < 128 bytes.
- Server maintains ephemeral resume anchors for 1 minute keyed by session id; anchors map to authoritative 'anchor_seq' and 'open_toolcall_marker'. Anchors stored in redis with max TTL and LRU eviction.
- Chunk framing: attach a 64-bit sequence number and a 16-bit fragment index per chunk. For JSON fragments belonging to a structured object, include 'struct-id' and 'frag-count' fields in chunk metadata.
- Idempotency: require tool calls to include idempotency_key when invoking external tool integrations; server will track idempotency_key -> completed_result mapping for the anchor window.
- Reconciliation path: server attempts to align client's last_seq against closest anchor. If convex match found, respond with minimal drop/append plan. If ambiguous, server responds with 'conservative_replay' instructing client to resend last N unacknowledged bytes.
- Keep heuristic merging on client limited and deterministic: prefer server-specified boundaries, otherwise drop partial trailing fragment if not parseable as JSON after merge attempt.
decisions:
- Chose hybrid snapshot+anchor approach over per-chunk persistent checkpoints to bound server state and reduce memory pressure.
- Sequence numbers are strictly increasing 64-bit integers to avoid rollover issues for long-lived sessions.
- Use a short TTL (1 minute) for resume anchors to balance availability vs memory. Longer TTLs increase stale state and cost.
- Fragment indexing chosen over length-prefixed payloads to preserve compatibility with existing SSE tooling and browsers.
- Opt-in header prevents breaking older clients; legacy behavior handled by fallback anchors without client hints.
- We will not attempt complex CRDT-style merges for toolcall outputs — too brittle for safety-critical function calls. Instead favor rollback-and-replay semantics for function-call atomicity.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for header parsing, anchor lookup logic, and server decision tree.
- Integration test harness simulating 10k clients with randomized reconnect intervals, packet loss, and out-of-order delivery. Validate no JSON structural corruption and toolcall atomicity.
- Fuzzing: generate fragmented JSON payloads across chunk boundaries to ensure client-side merge heuristics drop only trailing partial fragments.
- Load test: anchor traffic and redis eviction under 50k ephemeral anchors/minute to observe memory and latency impact.
- Upgrade tests: verify legacy clients (no snapshot) still receive a resume_anchor and can continue with conservative replay.
- Add Canary: enable feature for 5% of hosted traffic with detailed tracing and a rollback switch in Console if errors > threshold.
rollout_plan:
1) Internal dogfood with SDKs (node/python) for 2 weeks.
2) Canary: enable 5% of production traffic for runtime-2.3 with observability flags. Monitor replay rates, errors, and avg reconnect latency.
3) Expand to 25% after stability checks and positive metrics.
4) Full ramp and SDK docs/guides release.
5) Post-release 2 week observation window and quick patch path for any regressions.
Note: release gated on redis capacity bump and a small telemetry event to track anchor churn.
comments: 2026-02-11 Miguel Torres: Spike complete — implemented prototype for snapshot header encoder/decoder. Observed header sizes ~56 bytes for typical windows. Recorded in /docs/streaming/snapshots.md (internal).
2026-02-16 Asha Patel: Design review notes — prefer fragment-index over length-prefix to reduce client parsing complexity. Also requested clarifying behavior for garbage partial fragments.
2026-02-20 Design feedback (Priya Rao): UX for SDKs should expose automatic merge attempts with an opt-out. Keep merge attempts deterministic and limited to 1 retry.

2026-02-24 Security review (Ravi Singh): verified no sensitive data stored in anchors; anchors only contain seq and markers. Confirmed we must avoid storing full payload snippets. Security sign-off pending if anchors TTL <= 60s.

2026-03-02 Eng review (Daria Chen): Implemented server decision tree and added unit tests for ambiguous-anchor cases. Found edge where two anchors within same TTL conflicted due to multi-tab clients — added session scoping to anchors. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7821

2026-03-07 QA (Ben Ortiz): Integration harness shows ~0.03% of reconnect cases still produce a trailing partial json fragment that fails parse. Proposed change: on mismatch, server should instruct client to drop the last fragment and resume. Added test case.

2026-03-10 Miguel Torres: Addressed Ben's test by implementing explicit 'drop_last_fragment' flag in reconciliation response. Updated SDKs and added canary toggle. Moving to in-progress for canary rollout.
